summary: Four attacks, three of them clean and one low-severity finding. Every declaration the audit cites was re-read at the pinned commits: 528 claims (361 tauceti at f790474, 167 mathlib), and all 528 hold — the cited name is present in the cited file at the cited line, with no missing file, no absent name and no drifted line. The absence claims were tested against the libraries in both directions (PROTOCOL section 17's 'targets marked missing that the libraries have, or marked built that they lack') and are correctly drawn, including EnhancedDerivedSheaves' sweeping 'nothing homotopy-coherent in this roadmap exists', which is properly hedged and matches the tree. No duplication: across 280 targets in four roadmaps not one cross-roadmap pair overlaps materially, and the 11 declarations cited by two roadmaps are correct reuse of general library results, not mathematics planned twice. Layer coverage is complete: every layer heading in all four roadmap documents has an audit entry. One lead was investigated and dissolved rather than filed, and is recorded below in 'checked' so the next reader need not repeat it.
checked: Every declaration claim the audit makes, at the pinned commits: 528 claims extracted from every target of every layer (361 library=tauceti, 167 library=mathlib), each carrying name, library, file, line and fit; none lacked a file or a line.
The 361 tauceti claims verified with `git show f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369:<file>` and the cited name located within +/-3 lines of the cited line. 361 of 361 hold.

The 167 mathlib claims verified by locating the cited name within +/-5 lines of the cited line in the cited file. 167 of 167 hold. Caveat stated for the verifier: the mathlib tree available here is 30a58f79, not the pinned 082e2d3, so line drift would have been expected and excusable; there was none, and no cited name was absent from its file.

The absence direction, on EnhancedDerivedSheaves' summary claim that 'Nothing homotopy-coherent in this roadmap exists': probed the mathlib tree for the constructions it names and those it concedes. Quasicategory appears in 10 files, nerve in 27, SimplicialCategory in 6, Pretriangulated in 52, while dgNerve and StableCategory appear nowhere. That matches the summary's own division between the roadmap's homotopy-coherent content (absent) and 'the named starting points and their 1-categorical shadows' (present). Not an overclaim.

Duplication across the four roadmaps, by target text: all 280 targets pairwise compared across roadmap boundaries on content-word overlap. Zero pairs reach Jaccard 0.33. No two roadmaps state the same target.

Duplication by shared declaration: 11 declarations are cited under more than one roadmap. Each was inspected; all are correct reuse of a general result rather than duplicated planning. The one that looked wrong — TauCeti.leftRadical cited under both GrothendieckEulerForms and ProfiniteProPGroups — is correct: the profinite citation sits in the layer explicitly titled 'prerequisites: two owned inputs', whose input is bilinear forms over F_p.

Layer coverage against the four roadmap documents: layer headings extracted from content/tau-ceti/ProfiniteProPGroups/README.md (12 layers), content/campaign/EnhancedDerivedSheaves/README.md (E0-E5 plus five E5 sub-layers, 11), content/tau-ceti/DGAInfinity/README.md (12) and content/tau-ceti/GrothendieckEulerForms/README.md (8), and matched against the audit's layer keys. Every layer the documents define has an audit entry; the headings with no audit layer are prose sections (scope, conventions, worked examples, references).

The target-level 'library' field against the declarations under it, for all 280 targets. The field is a status field taking mathlib/tauceti/both/partial/absent, and it is used consistently: where it names a library, that library supplies the satisfying declarations; 'partial' marks a target only partly met; 'absent' marks a target the libraries lack, and the declarations listed under an 'absent' target document the nearest existing material rather than claiming satisfaction. Three targets named a library while citing only 'more general' declarations, and in each the note explains that the library result is strictly stronger and satisfies the target by instantiation (continuousCohomology in every degree; exists_continuous_section for any closed subgroup; cartanMap for any ring).

A lead investigated and dissolved, recorded so it is not repeated: whether layer verdicts are calibrated consistently. Tabulating all 43 layers by verdict against how many targets carry a satisfying declaration shows no 'partly built' layer without one, and three 'not built' layers with exactly one. Reading those three shows the audit is not applying a per-target rule but judging whether the layer's own subject is built, and in each case the satisfied target is flagged 'partial' with a note saying what is missing. The verdicts are defensible; only the presentational point in the single finding below survives.

findings.claim: Three layers carry verdict 'not built' although each contains one target that a library result already satisfies by instantiation. The verdicts are defensible as prose — in each case the layer's own subject is absent and the target is marked 'partial' with a note — but a downstream worker filtering on the machine-readable verdict alone cannot distinguish these three from the layers where nothing whatever exists, and so would miss reusable material. Two 'not built' layers (ProfiniteProPGroups layer 9, DGAInfinity layer 9) have zero targets with any declaration at all, which is the case the verdict reads naturally as.
findings.evidence: ProfiniteProPGroups layer 4, target 'Structure theorem A = Z_p^r x T for topologically finitely generated abelian pro-p groups' cites fit 'more general' mathlib Module.equiv_free_prod_directSum at Mathlib/Algebra/Module/PID.lean:257, with the note 'The algebraic structure theorem for finitely generated modules over a PID applies to Z_[p] (a DVR in Mathlib) but states existence only. Missing: uniqueness of r and of the elementary divisors, the pro-p/topological version, and the passage from abelian pro-p groups to Z_p-modules.' DGAInfinity layer 8, target 'A-infinity structures as degree-one square-zero coderivations over any commutative base' cites two fit 'exact' tauceti declarations, TauCeti.AInfinityAlgebra at TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/AInfinity/Algebra.lean:54 and TauCeti.AInfinity.IsSuspension.comp_self_eq_zero_iff_forall_stasheffSum_eq_zero at TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/AInfinity/Coderivation.lean:362; both read at f790474 and both present at those lines. DGAInfinity layer 10, target 'Left and right numerical quotients of K0(Perf C) by the radicals' cites fit 'more general' TauCeti.LeftNumericalQuotient at TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/SesquilinearForm/NumericalQuotient/Basic.lean:138 and TauCeti.numericalPairing_nondegenerate at :317. For contrast, DGAInfinity#layer-9-smoothness-properness-serre-and-calabi--yau and ProfiniteProPGroups#layer-9-the-classification-of-demushkin-groups have 0 of 5 and 0 of 7 targets with any declarations.
findings.fix: Leave the three verdicts as they are and make the reusable material visible at layer level: add a short 'reuse' note on each of the three layers naming the declaration a builder should start from (Module.equiv_free_prod_directSum; TauCeti.AInfinityAlgebra with comp_self_eq_zero_iff_forall_stasheffSum_eq_zero; TauCeti.LeftNumericalQuotient with numericalPairing_nondegenerate) and what it does not give. If the schema is to carry this instead, a distinct verdict value for 'subject absent but a general result instantiates part of it' would separate these three from the two layers with nothing at all.
